name: Zhou
place: the Wei valley and the warring states of the Yellow River
desc: The people who overthrew the Shang in the name of the Mandate of Heaven: rule belongs to the virtuous, and heaven takes it from the cruel. In their long decline, the warring states cast the first iron, built crossbows, and produced Confucius, Laozi, Sunzi and the Hundred Schools of thought.
source: The Book of Songs, the Book of Documents, the Zuo Zhuan; Western Zhou bronze inscriptions; excavated texts from Warring States tombs

devout: led the rites at the ancestral temple without a single misstep
belligerent: shot a crossbow bolt through a wooden shield at two hundred paces
cautious: poured molten iron into a mould for a ploughshare

inventions.name: Crossbow
inventions.source: Bronze crossbow trigger mechanisms appear in Warring States tombs from the 5th century BCE
inventions.desc: A bow on a stock with a bronze trigger, which anyone can shoot after a day's training: +3 attack.
inventions.hint: Needs Bronze Metallurgy and the Bronze & Mythic Era.

inventions.name: Cast Iron
inventions.source: Chinese smiths cast molten iron in moulds by the 5th century BCE, about two thousand years before Europe
inventions.desc: Iron melted in hot blast furnaces and poured like bronze into moulds for ploughshares and hoes: farm plots yield 15% more, woodcutting 10% faster.

inventions.name: The Book of Songs
inventions.source: 305 songs and odes of the Western Zhou and Spring and Autumn periods, said to have been chosen by Confucius
inventions.desc: Songs of love, work, war and the ancestors, gathered from every state: +3 mood, a little more lore.
inventions.hint: Needs the Tribe & Agrarian Era, and songs at the fire.

inventions.name: Rites and Music
inventions.source: The Duke of Zhou is credited with setting down the rites and music of the Zhou court; bronze bell sets like those of Marquis Yi of Zeng (433 BCE) played whole scales
inventions.desc: Every rite in its order, accompanied by bells of bronze tuned to every note: rites bring 10% more devotion, +2 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs Bronze Metallurgy, and long rites.

inventions.name: The Well-Field
inventions.source: Mencius described the 'well-field' system: nine plots like the character 井, eight families each farming one and sharing the work of the middle plot
inventions.desc: Land divided in nine squares, eight for families and one worked together for the common store: farm plots yield 10% more, +1 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs farming, and someone to lead.

foods.name: Fermented Paste
foods.source: The Rites of Zhou mention dozens of jiang, fermented pastes of meat, fish and beans
foods.desc: Beans or meat salted and left to ferment in sealed jars, to flavour everything: food spoils 10% slower, +1 mood.

foods.name: Pork for the Rites
foods.desc: Pork roasted and shared out after the offerings, each by rank: +3 mood.

finds.name: Wild Soybean
finds.desc: Twining vines with small hairy pods; the 'shu' of the old songs.

finds.name: Iron Sand
finds.desc: Heavy black sand in the river bends, full of iron.

people.name: Shi Ke
people.desc: He knows where every person should stand in every ceremony.
memory: sang the ode of King Wen at the ancestral temple

people.name: Jiang Ning
people.desc: She divides the land so no family has cause to complain.
memory: laid out nine fields like the sign for a well

people.name: King Wen
people.source: Book of Songs; Records of the Grand Historian; tradition credits him with arranging the hexagrams of the Book of Changes
people.desc: The virtuous lord of Zhou, imprisoned by the last Shang king, who is said to have arranged the sixty-four hexagrams of the Changes in prison.

people.name: The Duke of Zhou
people.source: Book of Documents; Confucius dreamed of him all his life
people.desc: The king's uncle who ruled for the boy-king, set down the rites and music, and gave the power back when the king came of age.

people.name: Laozi
people.source: Records of the Grand Historian: leaving for the west, he wrote the Daodejing for the keeper of the pass
people.text: an old archivist riding a black ox toward the western pass, who says he is leaving the world, but might stay a while.
memory: wrote five thousand words for the keeper of the pass and rode on
people.desc: The legendary author of the Daodejing, who taught that the soft overcomes the hard.

people.name: Confucius
people.label: Confucius the Teacher
people.desc: He teaches that a good ruler governs by example. Lore 9.

people.name: Sunzi
people.label: Sunzi, Master of War
people.desc: He wins battles without fighting them. Combat 8, Lore 6.

people.name: Mozi
people.label: Mozi, Defender of Cities
people.desc: An engineer who teaches love for all and builds defences for the weak. Crafting 8, Lore 6.

events.title: The Mandate of Heaven
events.source: The Zhou taught that heaven gives the right to rule to the virtuous and withdraws it, with floods, quakes and famine, from the wicked
events.text: After the earthquake people mutter that heaven is angry with the chief. The elders say: the mandate is not given forever. The chief must show virtue, or another will take it.

options.label: Open the granaries to the people
options.result: Grain goes to every household. The muttering stops: the chief still has the mandate.

options.label: Punish the mutterers
options.result: The mutterers fall silent. In their hearts, they wait.

events.title: The Beacon Fires
events.source: Records of the Grand Historian: King You lit the beacons to make his consort Bao Si laugh; when enemies really came, no one answered
events.text: The war chief has built beacon towers on the hills to call allies in danger. A young noble wants to light them for fun, to see the allies come running.

options.label: Light them, for a laugh
options.result: The allies come running and find nothing. Later, when the wolves come, the fires are lit again, and no one comes.

options.label: Beacons are not toys
options.result: The noble sulks. The beacons stay ready.

events.title: The Hundred Schools
events.source: In the Warring States period, Confucians, Mohists, Daoists, Legalists and many others argued at the courts of rival kings
events.text: Teachers have come from every state to argue in our square: one says rule by rites, one by love for all, one by doing nothing, one by strict laws. The young people listen all day.

tales.name: The Duke Who Held His Hair
tales.source: Records of the Grand Historian; Han Shi Waizhuan
tales.text: The Duke of Zhou was so eager to meet wise men that if one came while he was washing his hair, he would come out holding it in his hand; if one came while he was eating, he would spit out his food. He did this three times at one bath and three times at one meal.

tales.name: The Ospreys Cry
tales.source: Book of Songs, the first ode
tales.text: Guan guan cry the ospreys on the island in the river. The lovely, good young woman is a fit match for a gentleman. Long and short grow the floating-hearts; left and right we pick them. The lovely, good young woman: waking and sleeping he longs for her.
tales.moral: love is the beginning of all songs

tales.name: The Butterfly Dream
tales.text: Zhuang Zhou dreamed he was a butterfly, fluttering happily, not knowing he was Zhou. Then he woke, and was Zhou again. But he did not know whether he was Zhou who had dreamed of being a butterfly, or a butterfly now dreaming it was Zhou.
tales.moral: who can say what is real?

tales.name: Nothing Is Softer than Water
tales.text: Nothing under heaven is softer or weaker than water, the old master said, and yet nothing is better at wearing down the hard and strong. The weak overcomes the strong, the soft overcomes the hard. Everyone knows this; no one can put it into practice.
